ranges.purpose: list destructor including omitted native return tail
registry destructor, bucket storage before list destructor
range erase routing whole-list erase through clear

review_result: No blocking discrepancy found in the bounded storage/lifetime behavior; source review only.

verification.installed_saved_program_bytes: 16 complete address spans, 3444 bytes, all equal; not whole-program equivalence

findings.evidence: Sentinel allocation is 12 bytes, with next/previous at +0/+4; +8 is not written. Registry constructor allocates sentinel before 9 iterator pairs.
findings.source_result: Entry has next/previous/key only; sentinel payload preserves allocator bytes; attachment associations are in a separate host map with no ordering links.

findings.evidence: Each 8-byte iterator is {registry+4, link}; native list-owner+4 contains head and +8 contains size. Owner is not the address of its head-pointer field.
findings.source_result: Dedicated ListOwner contains an untouched leading DWORD, head and size; pairs use &list_. Win32 static assertions establish head +4 and size +8. Copies preserve the owner; link-only updates preserve an already-valid owner.

findings.evidence: General vector growth uses max(required, old_capacity + floor(old_capacity/2)), with 0x1fffffff limit; registry reachable lengths/capacities are 9,17,33,65,... . Split occurs before duplicate lookup.
findings.source_result: Private resize allocates the exact requested count. This equals native capacity for reachable registry growth; it is not a reconstruction of arbitrary vector insertion. Growth copies existing pairs, fills new pairs, frees old block, then publishes replacement storage.

findings.evidence: Clear first resets sentinel next/previous and size, then frees each entry, assigns 9 sentinel iterators without freeing capacity, and finally resets mask/active to 1. Whole-list erase routes through clear.
findings.source_result: Clear follows that logical order and retains boundary pointer/capacity. Subsequent regrowth within retained capacity reuses the block. Sentinel payload is untouched during clear.

findings.evidence: 00b828ca..00b828d5 unlinks the entry, 00b828d8 frees it, and returning continuation 00b828dd..00b828e3 decrements size. Borrowed key target is not freed.
findings.source_result: Entry unlink, free and size decrement remain in native order; host association is removed separately.

findings.evidence: Registry destructor frees/zeros iterator storage before entering list destructor. List destructor resets sentinel links and count before freeing entries, frees sentinel last, clears owner.head, and returns at 00b82a17.
findings.source_result: Destructor calls bucket-storage destruction first, then list destruction. List destruction follows reset/free/head-null order.

assembly_corrections_required_for_readin.meaning: Returning free continuation: stack cleanup, compare next against sentinel, loop, restore EDI.
Returning sentinel free continuation: stack cleanup, owner.head = null, restore ESI, RET at 00b82a17. Old Ghidra body ended at 00b82a0b.
Returning vector free continuation, followed by zeroing vector pointers and tail call to list destructor.
Returning old-vector free continuation, followed by publishing replacement capacity/end/begin.

limitations: The reconstructed C++ interface is not an object overlay or a drop-in x86 ABI replacement.
This review establishes source/data/order correspondence on well-formed registry state, not identical native exception handling or instruction-level store timing.
Host association storage has independent allocations; it is not part of the raw native list and is not asserted to reproduce a whole-process allocation trace.
Owner fields are invariant in the encapsulated interface; native validation and repair behavior for externally corrupted iterator owners is not reproduced.
Native sentinel +8 is unwritten. Reconstruction preserves its bytes via a read-and-write of the payload; identical memory-write traces are not claimed.
No existing focused registry native fixture was found in this checkout. This review adds no substitute native calls or broad tests.
